items.description: Position: Security Engineer II Reports To: Senior Manager, Security Engineering Department: Deployment Engineering, Microsoft Location: Remote, US Work Authorization: US Citizenship Required BlueVoyant is seeking a Security Engineer II to join our Deployment Engineering team, focused on enabling our Managed Detection and Response (MDR) solutions in customer environments. This fully remote role uses your expertise in Microsoft Cloud security technologies and SIEM platforms to lead client-facing SIEM and XDR technical enablement projects, including hands-on deployment of a broad range of Microsoft Security and Azure solutions. What You’ll Do: Deliver Microsoft Sentinel and Defender implementations for customers remotely, from design and architecture through deployment and use case tuning. Create and develop new detection, automation, and reporting use cases based on customer requirements. Define and assist in building operational and executive security reports and dashboards. Lead XDR integration activities across the Microsoft and Azure product stacks, applying Microsoft XDR and Zero Trust Architecture principles. Serve as the lead technical delivery resource within a team for small to large client-facing projects. Participate in research and development activities to drive process improvement and new product and feature enhancements. Support client-facing environments on an ongoing basis to help mature and maintain our MDR practices. What You’ll Bring: 5+ years of technical experience with Microsoft Cloud Security technologies or equivalent SIEM and XDR solutions. Hands-on experience deploying and/or managing Microsoft Sentinel. Hands-on experience deploying and/or managing Microsoft Defender security products (e.g., Defender for Endpoint, Identity, Cloud Apps, Office 365, Defender for Cloud). Hands-on engineering experience with SIEM and/or XDR technologies in production environments. Strong experience with Azure Cloud technologies. Experience with query languages and/or script development (KQL, SPL, SQL, PowerShell, or similar). Knowledge of enterprise IT systems as they relate to cybersecurity. Familiarity with Microsoft XDR and Zero Trust Architecture models. Excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced team environment. Nice to Have: Expertise in Kusto Query Language (KQL), including Sentinel Analytic Rules and Defender Custom Detection Rules. Expertise in Azure Logic Apps, Function Apps, and other Azure technologies. Experience in customer-facing roles. Incident investigation and response skills. Proficiency in Python, PowerShell, or C#/.NET. Proficiency in Linux configuration and common administration tasks. Experience with non-Microsoft SIEM or EDR tools. Education: Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent professional experience and certifications. Relevant Microsoft certifications (e.g., SC-200, AZ-500) are a plus. Why BlueVoyant? Lead hands-on Microsoft Sentinel, Defender, and Azure deployments that directly shape how customers detect and respond to threats. Work at the intersection of cloud security engineering, detection content, and customer delivery, building scalable solutions across diverse enterprise environments. Join a global, mission-driven cybersecurity company defending organizations worldwide with cutting-edge data, technology, and expertise. Competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package, with support for wellbeing, development, and career growth. About BlueVoyant BlueVoyant is an AI-driven cybersecurity company dedicated to standing between our customers and cyber threats. By combining human, artificial, and proprietary intelligence, we deliver a unified solution that protects every organization’s network, identities, vendors, and digital footprints as a single attack surface. The company’s award-winning Microsoft Security expertise helps organizations maximize their security investments while reducing risk and ensuring compliance. Led by CEO, John Hernandez, BlueVoyant’s highly skilled team includes former government cyber officials with extensive frontline experience in responding to advanced cyber threats on behalf of the National Security Agency, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Unit 8200, and GCHQ, together with private sector experts. BlueVoyant services utilize large real-time datasets with industry leading analytics and technologies. Founded in 2017 by Fortune 500 executives, including Chairman of the Board, Jim Rosenthal, Vice Chairman, Tom Glocer, and former Government cyber officials, BlueVoyant is headquartered in New York City and has offices in Maryland, Tel Aviv, London, Budapest, and Latin America and is committed to building a workplace where talented people are empowered to do their best work in the fight against global cyber threats. All employees must be authorized to work in the United States of America. BlueVoyant provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, BlueVoyant complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. Disclaimer: Please note that pursuant to contractual requirements and applicable law, for employees to perform work on some of the company’s federal contracts, U.S. citizenship is required. Accordingly, an employee’s ability to perform work on such contracts is contingent upon the company’s verification of the employee’s citizenship status. #LI-AH1 #LI-Remote Important Information for Applicants: BlueVoyant uses AI-assisted tools within our applicant tracking system to help identify candidates whose experience and skills best match the requirements of a role. This technology provides hiring teams with added insights to support fair and efficient hiring decisions. All applications are reviewed by a member of our hiring team, and final hiring decisions are made by humans, not AI. By submitting your application, you acknowledge that AI tools may assist in the evaluation of your resume as part of the recruitment process. Interview Expectations: As part of our interview process, we assess your experience through real-time discussion, so we expect responses to be your own. While we embrace the use of AI within our business and recruitment process, we do not permit its use during interviews. Any suspected use of AI during an interview will be challenged, and this may include the use of detection tools. BlueVoyant Candidate Privacy Notice: To understand how we secure and manage your personal data upon submitting a job application, please see our Candidate Privacy Notice, which can be found here - Candidate Privacy Notice

items.summary: At Vio we believe booking accommodation should feel smart, fair, and effortless — never overwhelming or unclear. As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the wo
items.description: At Vio we believe booking accommodation should feel smart, fair, and effortless — never overwhelming or unclear. As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the world. We cut through the noise and complexity of hotel and vacation rental booking, surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays — booked with confidence. With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology travelers can trust. Who we're looking for We are looking for a hands-on Quality Platform Lead to own Vio's quality strategy and automation platform across web, mobile, browser extensions, internal tooling and related surfaces. This is a technical leadership role (Staff IC) reporting to the Director of Engineering. You define what good looks like for quality, decide where scarce testing effort goes, and give teams the confidence to ship. Your levers are release gates, quality telemetry, and a developer experience that makes the right tests easy to write and keep alive. Product engineers own the tests for the features they build. Your remit is the platform, the strategy and the enablement that make that work hold up at scale. There is no QA department here and we have no plans to create one. Where you'll start Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack Mobile: Patrol (Flutter) Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack Mobile: Patrol (Flutter) Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling The tooling can stay as it is. With a clear case you can migrate or rebuild. E2E coverage today is thin, so a different platform is genuinely on the table if it serves speed, maintainability and DX better. We have no predefined answer. AI-assisted tooling is an open area too. We have no established practice for agent-generated tests or AI-assisted triage, so your judgment on what earns a place in the platform carries real weight. What we lack today is clear ownership of strategy, release gates and shared quality telemetry, plus a low-friction path for engineers to spend their testing effort on the highest-risk scenarios. How the role works Your time splits between hands-on platform work, enablement, strategy and stakeholder telemetry. One insourced QA Engineer supports you. You own the technical direction, the standards and the quality outcomes. Once the platform has low friction, product engineers write and maintain the tests for the domains they own. You enable that through patterns, docs, reusable modules, CI checks and risk-based guidance. Gatekeeping releases sits outside the role. Expect no direct people-management responsibilities in the near future. Any further QE hire gets evaluated against the ~1:50 rule once the value is proven, and we have no committed headcount plan beyond that. What you'll own Quality strategy and platform Own the quality strategy and the automation platform across products, covering direction, standards and day-to-day health Decide whether to keep, evolve or replace the current tooling, with clear trade-offs on speed, maintainability and DX Set coding standards and patterns for test code, and keep the suite focused on the tests that earn their place Release gates and telemetry Build automated release gates into CI/CD and define what protects the core journeys Give Product, Engineering and leadership real-time quality telemetry on release readiness, risk and pipeline health Put failure triage and flaky-test quarantine in place, so every failure is worth acting on Risk-based coverage and testability Work with Product and Engineering to protect high-impact journeys and APIs Retire flaky and low-value tests, and concentrate effort where the risk is highest Act as the technical stakeholder for testability (hooks, mocks, contract tests, test data) and get those improvements onto team roadmaps Developer enablement Make it easy for product engineers to write, run and maintain tests locally and in CI Embed quality into how teams plan and ship, and mentor the insourced QA Engineer Drive a measurable increase in developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX What success looks like in 12 months Platform ownership. You have taken over the automation platform across products and own it outright, with direction, standards and health all unambiguous, whether you kept the tooling or replaced it. Gates and focus. Release gates on the core journeys are fast and deterministic, and testing effort sits on the highest-risk scenarios. Dev ownership and satisfaction. Writing and maintaining tests is a routine part of Definition of Done, and developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX has measurably improved. Telemetry. Eng and Product work from live release-readiness and risk dashboards, failures triage cleanly, and flaky tests go into quarantine. Less manual drag. Regular releases go out without manual testing, with exploratory testing reserved for major new work. Who you are You have a track record of building or overhauling automation platforms (SWE / QE / SDET) You write production-grade code across app, test and infra repos. Language matters less to us than depth, though our stack today leans on TypeScript/JS, Elixir, Go, Python and Dart. You use AI agents effectively in your own engineering workflow and can judge where they belong inside a quality platform, from test generation to failure triage You have cross-platform web and mobile automation judgment, and can weigh unified toolchains against separate ones objectively You have deep CI/CD and test infrastructure experience: GitHub Actions, device clouds, parallelisation, test data You can translate quality risk into telemetry and decisions that Eng, Product and leadership act on You are a hands-on builder who wants to code the platform yourself You design platforms developers adopt, and you prioritise risk-based coverage Trade-offs we accept: depth on one platform when the other is learnable, and no travel or booking domain background. Why join us now? Full ownership of the quality strategy and the automation platform, with a mandate for enablement We are one of the most innovative and fastest-growing accommodation booking platforms in the world today, having grown our bookings 30x between 2017 and 2025, and catering to the needs of over 100 million unique visitors worldwide each year. We do that by harnessing the power of advanced algorithms and an innovative suite of power features and managed to overcome the corona crisis remarkably fast ; The mobile applications ( iOS and Android ) we launched in 2023 are already a big success, reaching 5 million installs with great customer reviews, as we are beginning to build Vio as the brand for value-seeking travellers worldwide; We are a passionate and diverse team of tech enthusiasts and creatives with a commitment and focus on the traveler above all else - and it shows in our industry-leading TrustPilot score ; We place huge importance on rewarding our employees for the value they generate by giving Stock Appreciation Rights to all employees. Do you want to know if Vio is the right place for you? Find out by reading about the attitude that thrives at Vio. What we offer: Plenty of chances to learn and grow within an open, diverse culture which promotes knowledge sharing, trust and transparency; A great compensation package, perks and benefits (including significant stock appreciation rights); Flexible time off (take as many holidays as you need) and a chance to work remotely; You will be part of a highly international team that enjoys working, eating and playing together in one of the best office locations in Amsterdam; We value good food and offer catered lunches from various cuisines, great coffee, and the occasional barbecue in our garden; We enjoy getting together to celebrate our wins with company events in Amsterdam and abroad; A budget for your dream home office; Access to free mental health support via OpenUp . Find more English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

items.description: About this Role Location: Remote (Global) Type: Volunteer, Pro bono Commitment: 10 – 15 hours a week, minimum of three months Reports To: Head of People Operations Works Closely With: Team Leads, Department Heads, People Team Position Summary Solution Community seeks a strategic, data-driven Volunteer Retention Manager to lead the organization's volunteer engagement and retention strategy. This role ensures volunteers remain connected, engaged, productive, and supported throughout their volunteer journey. The Volunteer Retention Manager serves as the central partner between the People Team and functional Team Leads, helping establish a culture where volunteer success and retention are shared responsibilities across the organization. The successful candidate will develop retention initiatives, oversee volunteer engagement analytics, identify attrition risks, support Team Leads in managing volunteers effectively, and create systems that improve volunteer satisfaction, productivity, and long-term commitment. This position combines workforce analytics, relationship management, volunteer experience design, and organizational development. Why This Role Matters At Solution Community , volunteer retention is not solely the responsibility of the People Team. Volunteers remain engaged when they experience meaningful work, effective leadership, consistent communication, recognition, and opportunities to contribute. Team Leads shape those experiences daily, while the People Team provides the systems, processes, and support that enable success. The Volunteer Retention Manager ensures both groups work together to create an environment where volunteers thrive, contribute, and remain connected to the mission over time. Key Responsibilities Volunteer Retention Strategy Develop and implement organization-wide volunteer retention strategies. Create programs that improve volunteer engagement and long-term participation. Monitor volunteer lifecycle trends from onboarding through ongoing engagement. Establish retention goals and success indicators across departments. Recommend improvements to volunteer processes, policies, and experiences. Volunteer Engagement Analytics Manage volunteer engagement and retention reporting. Analyze volunteer participation, activity levels, and engagement trends. Monitor Volunteer Health Indicators (Green, Yellow, Red). Identify volunteers at risk of disengagement and coordinate intervention plans. Produce monthly and quarterly retention reports for leadership. Track key metrics including: Retention Rate Volunteer Lifespan Engagement Scores Check-In Completion Rates Time to First Assignment Team Lead Effectiveness Metrics Partnership with Team Leads Act as the primary retention advisor to Team Leads. Support Team Leads in developing engagement plans for volunteers. Ensure volunteers receive proper onboarding, team integration, assignments, and recognition. Monitor completion of regular volunteer check-ins. Assist Team Leads in addressing volunteer concerns and performance challenges. Share best practices for volunteer engagement and development. Develop and maintain asynchronous volunteer management resources for Team Leads, including training videos, playbooks, toolkits, templates, guides, and best-practice documentation. Volunteer Experience Management Design initiatives that strengthen volunteer belonging and connection. Develop recognition and appreciation programs. Create volunteer feedback mechanisms and pulse surveys. Monitor volunteer satisfaction throughout the volunteer lifecycle. Identify barriers that may hinder volunteer participation and contribution. Recommend solutions that improve volunteer experiences across departments. Attrition Prevention and Intervention Develop early warning systems that identify volunteers at risk of disengagement. Review engagement indicators and trends to proactively address issues. Coordinate intervention plans with Team Leads. Conduct retention interviews with volunteers showing signs of disengagement. Lead efforts to recover and re-engage inactive volunteers when appropriate. Exit Analytics and Continuous Improvement Conduct and analyze volunteer exit interviews. Identify organizational, leadership, and role-related causes of attrition. Develop recommendations based on exit trends. Present findings and retention improvement opportunities to leadership. Track implementation of corrective actions. Leadership Reporting Prepare executive-level dashboards and retention reports. Present retention insights to leadership teams. Identify high-performing teams and engagement best practices. Highlight departments that require additional support. Support data-driven decision-making regarding volunteer management. Required Qualifications Experience in volunteer management, talent management, employee engagement, HR, organizational development, community management, or related fields. Strong analytical and reporting skills. Experience working with volunteer, workforce, or people analytics. Ability to build relationships across diverse teams and functions. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Experience designing engagement or retention programs. Strong problem-solving and project management abilities. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing large volunteer communities in a nonprofit setting. Familiarity with volunteer lifecycle management. Knowledge of workforce analytics and dashboard reporting. Experience using Airtable, Power BI, Excel, or similar reporting platforms. Experience leading cross-functional engagement initiatives. Core Competencies Volunteer Experience Management Stakeholder Partnership Data Analysis & Reporting Engagement Strategy Retention Planning Change Management Relationship Building Coaching & Advising Continuous Improvement Strategic Thinking Success Measures (KPIs) The Volunteer Retention Manager will be measured on: Volunteer Outcomes 30-, 60-, and 90-day retention rates Volunteer engagement scores Volunteer satisfaction results Volunteer re-engagement rates Reduction in preventable attrition Team Lead Accountability Measures Monthly check-in completion rates Volunteer assignment completion rates Volunteer health status trends Recognition activity rates Team-specific retention performance Organizational Measures Improvement in overall retention rates Reduction in volunteer inactivity Increased volunteer participation levels Increased average volunteer lifespan Improved volunteer experience scores What We Offer Global collaboration with leaders and strategists from top global companies. Meaningful impact on global causes and communities. A vibrant, multicultural team spanning 70+ countries. A supportive environment rooted in compassion, integrity, innovation, and collaboration. Flexible work-life with full autonomy. Opportunities for personal and professional growth. A formal recommendation upon successful completion of your volunteer term. Originally posted on Himalayas

items.description: Design Headquarters: Remote US At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most. About the Risk & Analytics Team The Risk & Analytics (R&A) team makes crucial decisions that direct Affirm’s business strategy. We partner with Machine Learning, Product, Engineering, Capital Markets, and Commercial teams to grow Affirm responsibly by optimizing approval, conversion, losses, and profitability. Operating across the entire customer and merchant lifecycle, we tackle a diverse array of challenges, from optimizing checkout conversion and mitigating fraud risk to building scalable data foundations and enabling international growth. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools, scalable data infrastructure, and analytical frameworks. We improve the analytics experience across Affirm by streamlining workflows and fostering a culture of learning and documentation. By taking ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, we turn complex data and systems into clear, actionable signals that ensure Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently. One Role, Multiple Teams We are hiring multiple Analyst I roles across Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across R&A. If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process. Potential team placements include: Point of Sale (POS): Optimize merchant and checkout performance to improve conversion, approvals, and unit economics across the purchase funnel. Direct to Consumer (DTC) / Card: Drive engagement, repeat usage, and lifecycle health across Affirm's app, web, and card experiences. Fraud: Prevent and reduce fraud losses across the customer journey while maintaining a frictionless user experience. Core Analytics: Build the quantitative research, machine learning models, performance monitoring, and scalable data foundations that enable fast, economically sound decisions. Servicing: Enhance the post-origination customer experience by analyzing repayment behavior, collections strategies, and operational efficiency. International Expansion: Build the measurement and decision foundations needed to sustainably launch and scale Affirm in new global markets. About the Role As an Analyst I in Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization, you will join one of several analytical teams working across the customer and merchant lifecycle. While the specific problems you tackle will depend on your eventual team placement, all Analyst I roles share a common foundation: using data to understand business performance, identify opportunities, and help Affirm make better decisions. You will learn the fundamentals of consumer lending while executing scoped analytical work under the guidance of senior analysts and managers. You will leverage SQL, Python, and modern analytical tools to help optimize business strategies, monitor performance, and turn complex data into actionable insights. You are a thoughtful, driven individual eager to build a strong technical foundation, learn how to navigate exogenous market changes, and integrate modern AI tooling to solve hard problems efficiently. What You Will Do Derive Insights & Support Strategy: Leverage data analytics to uncover insights that help optimize product, risk, or growth strategies across geographies. Monitor Portfolio Health: Assist in tracking performance metrics, user behavior, and macroeconomic trends that impact business outcomes, flagging risks and anomalies to senior team members. Technical Execution: Write clean, working SQL and Python to build scalable reporting and partner with Engineering to support the deployment of machine learning and risk models. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Product, Legal, and Compliance to understand evolving consumer lending regulations and market requirements, assisting in translating them into foundational data models and operational policies. Drive Launch Alignment: Support cross-functional discussions to ensure new product launches and market entries align with our operational capabilities and risk appetite. AI Fluency & Efficiency: Integrate AI tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, and copilots into your daily workflows to accelerate data mining and routine tasks, while carefully verifying outputs. What We Look For 1–3 years of experience in an analytically driven role. Relevant internships or prior experience in consumer lending, fintech, or the broader financial services industry are highly valued. Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative field. Solid working knowledge of SQL, Python, or other scripting languages. Familiarity with data mining, data visualization, and foundational statistical modeling. Basic understanding of, or deep curiosity about, consumer lending regulations, fair lending principles, and how machine learning techniques apply to real-world business problems. Exceptional communication skills, humility, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional peers. Pay Grade - I Equity Grade - 5 Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range . Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company). USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $115,000 - $165,000 USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $101,000 - $151,000 #LI-Remote Remote-first with flexibility built in Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience. Benefits designed for you Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights: Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents. Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you. Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to. Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount. We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help. For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law. By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/affirm-analyst

items.description: Sales and Marketing Headquarters: Netherlands URL: https://www.testgorilla.com/careers ✨ Where do we hire from? Find out if we're hiring in your location from hiring at TestGorilla Hi there, I'm Mehak , interim Head of Marketing at TestGorilla. We’re excited to share more about the Sr. Demand Generation Manager role and our team. About the role As our Sr. Demand Generation Manager , you'll be essential in achieving TestGorilla's vision of helping one billion people land their dream job. You'll own our largest acquisition lever, a multi-six-figure monthly Google Ads investment, along with the lifecycle, enrichment, and website systems that turn that spend into revenue. This isn't just a role, it's your chance to make a real difference by proving, with data, that every dollar of spend becomes pipeline. You'll directly contribute to sustainable, cost-efficient growth as TestGorilla scales. Responsibilities In this role, your responsibilities will include but not limited to: Upholding TestGorilla's behaviors and fostering an inclusive, supportive culture. Owning the demand generation number across paid and organic channels, including managing and scaling paid spend across Google Ads (Search, Performance Max, Display, YouTube) and adjacent channels, while testing and developing emerging acquisition opportunities such as advertising on ChatGPT and other AI-native platforms. Setting the channel mix, budget allocation, and account structure required to hit MQL, SQO, and pipeline targets. Building and owning source-of-truth reporting across paid and organic funnel performance, including SQL, dashboards, attribution modeling, and incrementality testing, so channel investment decisions are backed by evidence rather than platform screenshots. Owning the roadmap for paid landing pages, ad creative, and offers, and running rapid A/B tests to lift conversion with proper statistical rigor. Designing and owning automated nurture workflows and enrichment infrastructure (n8n, Make, HubSpot, Clay) so paid-sourced leads convert, and feeding that data back into targeting and ICP decisions. Partnering with Sales and RevOps on lead quality and conversion by campaign, and presenting performance and recommendations to marketing and GTM leadership in clear, business-first language. Staying ahead of advertising platform, AI ecosystem, and privacy changes, and turning successful tests into repeatable, automated systems rather than one-off wins. What you’ll bring We're looking for someone who: Is passionate about TestGorilla's mission to help one billion people find their dream jobs. Has excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Thrives in a fast-paced, async-first, remote-only environment. Has proven experience in performance or growth marketing, including hands-on ownership of a Google Ads budget of at least six figures per month (B2B SaaS strongly preferred), and a track record of scaling spend while holding or improving CAC and ROAS. We typically expect 7+ years of experience in performance or growth marketing to have developed the core skills necessary for this position. But it may be more or less than that, according to your career journey so far. Has deep expertise across the Google Ads stack, including Search, Performance Max, Display, YouTube, Smart Bidding, conversion tracking, and Google Tag Manager. Working knowledge and hands-on expertise of Clay, HubSpot (or a comparable CRM) and GA suite. Has a solid grasp of funnel and unit economics (CAC, LTV:CAC, ROAS, payback period, cohort analysis) and comfort with experimentation design, including significance, sample sizing, and reading results honestly. Has hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) to build real growth workflows, from lead scoring to automation logic, not just surface-level use. Has an ownership mentality: treats this budget like their own P&L, ships the workflow, dashboard, and test themselves, and is comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration as pipeline needs shift. We seek diversity and encourage applications from everyone. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups can be hesitant to apply unless they meet every requirement. If you're interested in this role but your experience doesn't perfectly match the description, please still apply. Bonus skills While these skills aren’t a requirement, we’d be very interested to hear from you if you have: Experience managing an agency or freelancers alongside in-house execution. Exposure to PLG or hybrid PLG/sales-led GTM. Experience presenting to VP/C-level stakeholders on performance and budget. Experience owning SEO or content-led demand generation programs alongside paid channels. Has strong working SQL, fluency in GA4 and at least one BI tool What’s in it for you? Please note: Some specifics, particularly around leave, may vary depending on your country of residence. This will be discussed during the hiring process. Global Team: Join a fully remote, mission-driven team from around the world Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive pay (€65,650-€84,500 per annum) + Share Appreciation Rights (SARs) Remote & flexible work: Work from almost anywhere*. Enjoy flexible hours and asynchronous work to balance work and life. * Check out the countries we currently hire from here Remote work budget: €1,000 available each year or up to €2,000 from day 1 if you're buying a laptop! Growth & development: Invest in yourself and your career with a 3.5% L&D budget per year and clear growth opportunities Parent/Caregiver support: We provide a caregiver-friendly work environment with paid 8-16 week parental leave and tailored return-to-work approaches Work-life balance: Our unlimited and flexible time off policy empowers you to take the time you need to recharge and maintain your well-being Interested? At TestGorilla, we believe your skills speak louder than your resume. That's why we champion a skills-first approach, using cutting-edge, AI-powered assessments to uncover your true potential. Forget traditional biases; we're building the world's largest skills-tested talent pool, making hiring fairer, faster, and smarter for everyone! When you apply, you'll get to experience our platform firsthand by taking an assessment – it's your chance to shine and show us what you can do! While our platform is powered by AI, every hiring decision is made by humans, ensuring a truly unbiased and thoughtful process. Check out our Applicant Privacy document to see how we protect your data. We're passionate about building diverse teams where every voice is heard. We genuinely welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences. Concerned about test anxiety? We've got you covered. Accommodations are readily available as part of the assessment setup, and requesting support will never impact your application. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/testgorilla-senior-demand-generation-manager

About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is…
items.description: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. At 1Password, we believe everyone deserves to be safe online. As a Senior GTM Engineering Analyst, you’ll build artificial intelligence (AI) agents, data products, and analysis workflows that help global go-to-market teams work faster and make better decisions. You’ll connect information across business systems, automate repetitive processes, and create reliable insights for leaders across Sales, Solutions, Customer Experience, and Channel. Your work will help make security simpler and more human-centric for the millions of people and thousands of businesses that rely on 1Password. This role reports to the Director, GTM Engineering (Revenue Operations) How we’re using AI today Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here. This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US. Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. What we're looking for: • Bring 4+ years of experience in analytics, revenue operations, sales operations, data analysis, or a related field. • Have experience building AI agents or workflows powered by large language models (LLMs) that have been used in real business work. • Work confidently with AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. • Use Structured Query Language (SQL) effectively and apply working knowledge of statistics to distinguish meaningful results from noise. • Document and improve business processes with a focus on reducing manual work and improving decision-making. Bonus points for: • Have experience with Python for building automations, working with application programming interfaces (APIs), and connecting systems, along with go-to-market tools such as Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, or business intelligence platforms. • Have supported channel or partner sales motions, worked across multiple regions, or studied a quantitative discipline such as science, engineering, statistics, or mathematics. What you can expect: • Rebuild sales and revenue operations processes to reduce manual work. • Build and maintain AI agents that prepare call and deal briefs, draft customer follow-ups, rank target accounts, and flag deals that need attention. • Build and maintain data tables and scheduled analysis jobs that combine information from Salesforce, Gong, and other go-to-market systems. • Create reports, alerts, and weekly manager briefs used by sales leadership. • Partner with Sales, Solutions, Customer Experience, Channel, and Revenue Operations teams to understand business needs and define clear technical requirements. • Map existing go-to-market processes, identify opportunities to improve data quality and efficiency, and help teams make better decisions. • Evaluate AI-generated outputs for quality, accuracy, privacy, data access, and appropriate safeguards; measure adoption and effectiveness, then improve workflows based on feedback and results. USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $113,000 USD and $158,000 USD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $105,000 CAD and $147,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Our culture At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. How we work with AI We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password. This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others. Our approach to work We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement. For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average. Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. What we offer We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: Health and wellbeing Maternity and parental leave top-up programs Competitive health benefits Generous PTO policy Growth and future RSU program for most employees Retirement matching program Free 1Password account Community Paid volunteer days Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly Remote-first work environment *Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting. You belong here. 1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love. Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs. Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you. Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law. 1Password uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies, including natural language processing and predictive analytics, to assist in the initial screening of employment applications and improve our recruitment process. See here for the latest third party bias audit information. If you prefer not to have your application assessed using AI/ML features, you may opt out by completing this form . For additional information see our Candidate Privacy Notice .

Cost Management: Monitor and analyze costs associated with division operations, identify cost-saving opportunities, and provide recommendations for optimization. Performance Metrics: Develop and maintain key performance indicators (KPIs) for the assigned operating division(s), tracking financial performance against targets in conjunction with Global Shared Services. items.description: Principal AI Solutions Consultant Our client is a healthcare organization specializing in Patient Support Programs, looking for a Principal AI Solutions Consultant to join their team on a contract basis. This is a practical, results-driven role focused on developing AI-powered automations and MVP solutions that streamline operations and enhance program visibility. In this role, the Consultant will partner with Project Managers, Operations, and Clinical teams to turn real operational challenges into effective, user-friendly tools built on Microsoft 365, Power Platform, and large language models. Note that compliance, pharmacovigilance, DPIA, and patient data handling fall outside the scope of this role — those responsibilities sit entirely with the client's internal teams. What You'll Be Doing The Consultant will own the end-to-end delivery of focused, high-value MVPs and automations across 2–3-week sprints, with structured demos and knowledge transfer at each cycle. The engagement will span across 6-8 weeks, and full-time work may be available after this period. Work will span: Building a Trust Engagement Database leveraging tools such as Notion, SharePoint, or equivalent platforms. Developing Power Automate workflows and Copilot Agent assets — covering prompt libraries, lightweight agent frameworks, automated SLA reminders, email and Teams-based triggers, tracking dashboards, and recurring or on-demand reporting. Prototyping LLM-assisted Adverse Event (AE) triage workflows (non-PHI), encompassing classification and summarization logic, intelligent routing, and retrieval from approved content sources. Wrapping up solutions as reusable, well-documented components: data models, deployment runbooks, and step-by-step how-to guides. Working hand-in-hand with Project Managers and Operations to make sure every solution lands well and can scale. Contributing to the client's AI-driven Digital Transformation initiatives. What We're Looking For Proven track record delivering production-ready automations within the Microsoft 365 ecosystem (SharePoint, Teams, Power Automate, Power BI). Hands-on experience working with LLM-based tools, prompts, or agent frameworks (Azure OpenAI, Copilot, Claude, or similar). Strong command of data modeling using Notion, Excel, CSV, and Microsoft Graph. History of shipping MVPs on tight, sprint-based timelines. Comfortable working in a contract/consultancy capacity. You must be available for 6 to 8 weeks of work, with the potential of staying on as a full-time staff member afterward. Background in pharma or healthcare — particularly familiarity with industry terminology — is a significant plus. Nice to Have Experience integrating HubSpot or Microsoft Graph into existing workflows. Knowledge of evaluation frameworks for classification and summarization tasks. A portfolio of reusable internal tooling built for external clients. Working Style & Values Able to navigate non-PHI environments confidently and responsibly. Highly organized with a sharp ability to prioritize under pressure. Thrives in dynamic, fast-moving settings. Our client is a values-driven organization in the healthcare space, guided by the principles of caring, candor, and high performance. They are seeking someone who welcomes feedback, adapts their approach based on team input, and brings both conviction and humility to collaborative problem-solving. if this sounds right for you, use the form below to apply! items.title: Service contract for endline population-based representative survey on menstrual
items.summary: I. GENERAL FRAMEWORK OF REFERENCE 1. 1 BackgroundFòs Feminista is an intersectional feminist organization centred around the sexual and reproductive rights and needs of women, girls, and gender-diverse people.
items.description: I. GENERAL FRAMEWORK OF REFERENCE 1.1 Background Fòs Feminista is an intersectional feminist organization centred around the sexual and reproductive rights and needs of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. Led and governed by the Global South, Fòs Feminista works as an alliance of organizations in 40+ countries worldwide to advance sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice. Fòs Feminista is both the connective tissue that links these diverse partners in an alliance and an active participant in the broader ecosystem of actors working on sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice (SRHRJ). Fòs Feminista orchestrates transnational and transregional action by connecting partners throughout the SRHRJ ecosystem, amplifying innovative partner-led solutions to SRHRJ issues, and catalysing funding and political will for an intersectional feminist agenda on SRHRJ. We recognize that the ability of women, girls, and gender-diverse people to make free and informed choices about their sexual and reproductive lives, including to access safe and legal abortion, is central to their life plans and to achieving gender and reproductive justice. Together with partners in the Alliance, we provide access to sexual and reproductive health care and services, including contraception, abortion, and care for victims of gender-based violence, and we reach young people with comprehensive sexuality education. We are at the forefront of advocating for sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice from an intersectional lens in national, regional, and global spaces, coordinating with our partners to ensure that diverse experiences, priorities, and voices of the Global South are represented in these spaces. We also strengthen intersectional feminist movements and organizations by creating and holding space for partners to participate in an international community built on feminist values of sharing power, diversity, mutual learning, and solidarity and to access resources to strengthen their work. Fòs Feminista is leading the Sang pour Sang consortium project to challenge the structural drivers of menstrual discrimination in nine countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean so that women, girls, and gender-diverse individuals have the information, services, products, infrastructure, and supporting environment to exercise their right to menstruate with dignity. Sang pour Sang is a consortium project of four international organisations. The project is funded by AFD (Agence Française de Développement) and has a duration of three years. II. SCOPE OF WORK 2.1 Objective & Role of the Consultancy The main objective of this consultancy is to design, conduct, and analyse the results of an endline population-based representative survey to measure changes from baseline in the structural factors of menstrual discrimination experienced by menstruators in the nine Sang pour Sang project countries: Benin, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Dominican Republic, Guinea, Haiti, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the Philippines. The endline population-based survey will replicate the baseline survey of menstruators methodology as closely as possible to ensure comparability of results over time, including consistency in the sampling approach, survey instrument, indicator definitions and calculations, data collection procedures, and analytical methods. Any necessary methodological changes will be agreed upon with Fòs Feminista , documented, and assessed during a pilot phase to assess their potential implications for comparability. The consultant will ensure a representative sample of the target population of menstruators in each country that is comparable to the baseline sample. In addition, the consultant will include a targeted sample of approximately 450 systematically excluded menstruators, approximately 50 per country, using selection criteria and survey approaches consistent with the baseline to ensure inclusivity. To maximize comparability with the baseline population-based survey of menstruators, the consultant will use the same or similar local survey partners and fieldwork networks where feasible. This will support the consultant in maintaining survey implementation procedures that are as consistent as possible with the baseline population-based survey. Required Endline Indicators The primary outcome of interest for the endline population-based survey is the prevalence of menstrual discrimination among menstruators. This outcome will be measured as the percentage of surveyed menstruators who report experiencing at least one restriction on regular activities during their last menstrual period and/or being teased about their menstrual period in the previous six months. The endline survey must also measure a set of key secondary outcomes aligned with core components of the Sang pour Sang project’s logical framework. The following indicators are required to measure the priority primary and secondary outcomes: Primary Outcome Indicator: Domain: Menstrual Health and Dignity Impacts % of menstruators who report menstrual discrimination % of menstruators whose participation in regular daily activities was restricted by their last period Factors that facilitated or prevented participation in regular activities during menstruation % of menstruators who experienced teasing related to menstruation in the last six months % who experienced teasing from men and boys Key Secondary Outcome Indicators: Domain: Knowledge and Awareness: % of menstruators who are aware of more than 1 type of menstrual product Domain: Product Use and Preference % of menstruators using purposely-made menstrual products from local social and solidarity enterprises (SSEs) Domain: Access to Menstrual Products % of menstruators who report that their preferred menstrual product is available and affordable $US in monthly cost per menstruator using menstrual products The endline survey must also measure the following supplementary indicators on important project domains and compare results against baseline: Domain: Knowledge and Awareness: % of menstruators with correct knowledge of the fertile period during the ovulatory cycle % of menstruators who know how often to change menstrual products % of individuals with knowledge of menopause Domain: Menstrual Attitudes % of menstruators who believe menstruation is dirty or impure % of menstruators who think menstruation should be discussed openly with everyone % of menstruators who believe that women are inferior to men because they menstruate % of menstruators who feel proud to menstruate Domain: Supportive Environment and Behaviors % of menstruators who believe that others in their community think that menstruation is dirty or impure % of menstruators who feel confident that they have the skills to manage their menstruation % of menstruators who would feel comfortable seeking help for menstrual problems from a health-care provider % of menstruators who report that they were able to reduce their menstrual (abdominal/back/cramping) pain when they needed to during their last menstrual period. % of menstruators who have someone they feel comfortable asking for support (advice, resources, emotional support) regarding menstruation Domain: WASH % of menstruators who had a space that was clean, private, and where they feel safe to change their menstrual materials during their last menstrual period % of menstruators who have consistent access to water for washing during menstruation % of menstruators who have hygienic options for disposal of used menstrual products Domain: Access to Menstrual Products % of menstruators who experienced barriers in having their need for menstrual products/materials met % of menstruators that used menstrual products during their last period, by type % of menstruators who are satisfied with their current method of management of their menstruation Qualitative reasoning for why menstruators are satisfied/dissatisfied with their current method of management of their menstruation Menstruators’ preference for menstrual materials by reusability/disposability % of menstruators who are open to using insertable menstrual materials % of menstruators who regularly experience difficulty managing their period due to a lack of adequate underwear % of menstruators who reported having enough menstrual materials during their last menstrual period % of menstruators who would use a different type of product if they could afford it % of menstruators who decide how much they pay for their menstrual products % of menstruators who are open to paying extra for menstrual products by factor All results must be disaggregated by country and age group, along with other factors relevant to the local context. An intersectional feminist lens is expected to be applied to all processes and deliverables. 2.2 Consultancy Deliverables In collaboration with the project consortium members, particularly the Business Intelligence, Evaluation & Research Cluster of Fòs Feminista , the contracted consultant will complete the following deliverables: - Inception report. The consultant will submit a brief inception report by December 15, 2026, outlining the proposed methodology for the endline survey, including the sampling strategy (with confirmation that replicating the baseline sample size provides adequate statistical power to detect meaningful change in the primary outcome, including at the country level), data collection approach, baseline-endline statistical comparison plan (including the approach to weighting and significance testing), and intersectional feminist analysis. The report will also include a work plan specifying key activities, timelines, and level of effort. The inception report will be subject to review and approval by Fòs Feminista . - Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval. Prior to the start of any data collection, the consultant must develop ethics procedures to protect respondents and obtain all required ethical approvals for the research. Documentation of IRB approval will be submitted to Fòs Feminista before December 31, 2026. - Documentation of methodological adjustments, pilot results, and finalized survey instruments. The consultant will document any proposed changes from the baseline methodology, including the rationale for each change and its potential implications for baseline-endline comparability. Proposed adjustments to the survey methods and instruments will be pretested with key informants and then pilot tested with a separate sample of menstruators in selected project countries to assess validity, appropriateness, and consistency with baseline measures. The deliverable will summarize the pilot methodology and findings, document any resulting revisions, and include the finalized survey instruments. This deliverable will be submitted by March 31, 2027. - Cleaned datasets and indicator calculations. By June 30, 2027, the consultant will submit complete, cleaned, deidentified, translated, and merged respondent-level datasets covering all nine countries, with all data provided in English. In addition to these respondent-level datasets, the consultant will provide the calculated result for each survey indicator, both overall and by country, based on the underlying respondent data. A codebook and calculation guide will document all indicator definitions, formulas, numerators, denominators, weighting procedures, derived variables, and the specific respondent-level variables used to calculate each indicator, together with any other information needed to reproduce each reported result. - Baseline-endline comparative findings report. By July 31, 2027, the consultant will submit one finalized report containing comparative analysis between endline and baseline data on respondents and the survey indicators. The report should describe the methodology and any limitations affecting comparability; assess the demographics of the surveyed menstruators at endline and how they compare to baseline; present changes in key indicators overall and by relevant subgroups; and include an intersectional feminist analysis of differences in findings across populations experiencing overlapping forms of discrimination and exclusion. This report should focus on providing an overall analysis of findings across all nine survey countries, followed by a brief analysis of main findings by country. All deliverables will be reviewed by Fòs Feminista and, as appropriate, relevant consortium partners. Deliverables should consistently apply an intersectional feminist lens and examine differences for people situated at the intersection of discriminatory power structures. Any translation or back translations needed to produce deliverables in English will be conducted by the consultant and their local networks. 2.3 Consultant Profile The ideal consultant has: Prior involvement in the design and implementation of the baseline population-based representative survey, with demonstrated capacity to replicate its methodology, instruments, sampling approach, and field procedures to ensure comparability between baseline and endline results. Fluent verbal and written communication skills in both English and French, with demonstrated ability to test and administer surveys in the local languages of Benin, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Dominican Republic, Guinea, Haiti, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the Philippines. Specialized expertise in population-based representative survey development, testing, and administration in the Global South, with a preference for survey experience in the 9 countries of the project. Extensive background in designing and implementing rigorous assessments of sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice, with the expertise to assess menstrual discrimination with an intersectional feminist lens. Demonstrated ability to incorporate ethical considerations and protections, as well as local adaptations of deliverables for each country. Strong knowledge of the sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice landscape in Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean, with a particular focus on menstrual health and dignity. Ability to collaborate effectively in multicultural settings across multiple time zones and using remote digital formats. Ability to adapt to challenges and opportunities as they arise. Familiarity with Agence Française de Développement requirements or reporting is a plus. III. INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENT 3.1 Project Duration All deliverables related to the endline survey shall be completed by July 31, 2027. 3.2 Work Location This consultancy will be conducted remotely, with the ability to apply the representative survey in Benin, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Dominican Republic, Guinea, Haiti, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the Philippines. The contracted consultant must be willing to adjust to different time zones. 3.3 Reporting The consultancy will report to Fòs Feminista 's Business Intelligence, Evaluation, and Research Unit. IV. APPLICATION PROCESS For consideration, please submit a résumé or portfolio that demonstrates expertise in representative survey development, implementation, and analysis, as well as a proposal for the consultancy. The proposal must include the proposed methodology and approach, anticipated level of effort and timelines for deliverables, and a financial offer in US dollars, which includes rates plus all taxes and liens that this type of consultancy requires. All application materials shall be submitted in English. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted. V. SAFEGUARDING COMMITMENTS Fòs Feminista is committed to ensuring that the health, rights, and wellbeing of all children, young people, and vulnerable populations who work and engage with Fòs Feminista 's Team Members and Associated Persons are respected and protected in their interactions with them, so it requires all its Team Members and Associated Persons to share this commitment. The successful consultant must: Sign and adhere to Fòs Feminista 's International Safeguarding Policy and Safeguarding Code of Conduct, including the minimum operating standards for protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). VI. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER STATEMENT Fòs Feminista provides equal opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to age, race, color, disability, national origin, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital and partnership status, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected category under federal, state, and local law. As an outsourcing and consulting partner, we do not have one specific client project lined up for you. Instead, you will be our technical anchor. If you are someone we can count on to solve complex problems and lead technical directions, we want you on our team. WE WILL REQUEST A VOICE NOTE FOR THE SCREENING PROCESS. Cloud Infrastructure: Strong hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles. System Design: Proven track record of designing distributed systems, APIs, and database schemas. Soft Skills Required: Excellent troubleshooting, problem-solving, and communication skills. Proactive and organized approach to project management. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote setting. Detail-oriented mindset with a focus on accuracy and quality. Ability to multitask and manage time effectively in a fast-paced environment. Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Strong documentation skills and attention to detail. Key Responsibilities: Architecture & Project Initiation Design robust system architectures for upcoming client projects, ensuring scalability, security, and performance. items.title: Backend / Full Stack Developer (Mid to Senior)
items.summary: Ψάχνουμε έναν/μια Backend Developer που να ξέρει το web σε βάθος.
items.description: Ψάχνουμε έναν/μια Backend Developer που να ξέρει το web σε βάθος. Θέλουμε κάποιον που καταλαβαίνει πώς ρέει ένα HTTP αίτημα μέσα από το σύστημα, μπορεί να σχεδιάσει καθαρό domain model, και να στήσει αρχιτεκτονική που δεν καταρρέει όταν μεγαλώνει. Το UI κομμάτι υπάρχει και το υποστηρίζουμε, αλλά αυτός ο ρόλος έχει ως επίκεντρο backend λογική, δομή δεδομένων, APIs και συστήματα που αντέχουν . Τι θα κάνεις Σχεδιασμό domain μοντέλων και βάσεων δεδομένων. Υλοποίηση APIs με καθαρή δομή και ξεκάθαρο separation of concerns. Εργασία πάνω σε business logic, pipelines, workflows και background processes. Βελτιστοποίηση απόδοσης, scaling patterns και monitoring. Συμμετοχή στον σχεδιασμό αρχιτεκτονικής και νέων υπηρεσιών. (Όταν χρειάζεται) συνεργασία με το frontend για να ορίζονται data contracts και component interfaces. Τι ζητάμε Πολυετή εμπειρία σε web development, με κύρια εστίαση στο backend. Βαθιά κατανόηση HTTP: request lifecycle, headers, caching, authentication flows. Ικανότητα να σχεδιάσεις data models και να γράψεις αποτελεσματικά SQL queries. Άνεση με full-stack ροή: όχι απαραίτητα να φτιάξεις UI, αλλά να καταλαβαίνεις όλη την εφαρμογή από άκρη σε άκρη. Εμπειρία στη συντήρηση και εξέλιξη production συστημάτων. Nice to have (όχι deal breakers) Εμπειρία σε Elixir και Phoenix. Εμπειρία με σύγχρονα frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte) ώστε να συνεργάζεσαι αποτελεσματικά. TailwindCSS familiarity Previous exposure σε distributed συστήματα, message queues ή event-driven αρχιτεκτονικές. Το stack μας PostgreSQL Elixir Phoenix Framework TypeScript TailwindCSS Τι προσφέρουμε Ρόλο με πραγματικό ownership και αυτονομία. Συμμετοχή σε τεχνικές αποφάσεις και shaping του συστήματος. Περιβάλλον χωρίς περιττές διαδικασίες και micromanagement. Ρυθμό που επιτρέπει να γράφεις καλό κώδικα, όχι απλά να τρέχεις tasks. Αν σε ενδιαφέρει να δουλεύεις σε συστήματα που έχουν ουσία, με καθαρό design και έμφαση στην απλότητα και την αξιοπιστία, κανε αίτηση και στείλε μας: Github / portfolio LinkedIn (αν υπάρχει) Μια σύντομη σημείωση για το τι σε ενδιαφέρει τεχνικά αυτή την περίοδο Originally posted on Himalayas

items.description: AST SpaceMobile is building the first and only global cellular broadband network in space to operate directly with standard, unmodified mobile devices based on our extensive IP and patent portfolio and designed for both commercial and government applications. Our engineers and space scientists are on a mission to eliminate the connectivity gaps faced by today’s five billion mobile subscribers and finally bring broadband to the billions who remain unconnected. Position Overview We are seeking an AI SaaS Product Manager to own the released application portfolio built in-house by the AI & Autonomy division — the AI-powered web, mobile, and spatial applications used daily by manufacturing, satellite operations, analytics, and executive teams, along with AI capabilities delivered to telecom partners. This person is the connective tissue between the engineers who build these applications, the internal customers who depend on them, and the IT organization that helps support them, deciding what ships next based on real usage and ensuring everything that ships is documented, learnable, and supportable. As the organization matures its operational support model for AI applications, this role also supports the Chief of AI and Autonomy in executing the transition roadmap that moves these applications from build-team support into steady-state operations. This is a hands-on, writing-heavy product role for someone fluent enough in AI/ML systems to document them accurately, and user-obsessed enough to measure success by adoption, time-to-resolution, and how rarely people need to ask for help. Key Responsibilities: Own the post-launch product lifecycle for the AI division’s released applications — prioritizing enhancements, defects, and retirements based on usage data, user feedback, and business impact — and maintain a published roadmap internal customers can plan against. Partner daily with the full-stack, ML, and data science engineering teams to translate user needs into clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria; participate in sprint planning, backlog grooming, and release readiness reviews. Run structured discovery with internal customers — quality inspectors, manufacturing engineers, satellite operations staff, analysts, and executives — through interviews, floor-side shadowing, and usage analytics, converting what you learn into prioritized product decisions. Define and track product success metrics for each released application (adoption, active usage, task completion, feature engagement, support volume, user satisfaction) and report them to the Chief of AI and Autonomy. Own release readiness as a gate: no application ships without release notes, updated user documentation, a known-issues list, and an agreed support plan. Write and maintain end-user product documentation for every released application — getting-started guides, workflow walkthroughs, feature references, administrator guides, and versioned release notes. Design and maintain in-app guidance: onboarding tours, contextual help, empty states, and error messaging written so users can self-correct without filing a ticket. Build and maintain the self-help troubleshooting library — a catalog of common errors, their causes, and step-by-step resolution paths mapped to actual error codes and failure modes, including AI-specific ones such as low-confidence predictions, model timeouts, and degraded offline sync. Partner with engineering to ensure errors are instrumented, human-readable, and traceable, turning raw exceptions and API failures into diagnosable user-facing messages with documented remediation steps. Co-own the support model with Corporate IT: define tiering and escalation paths, write the IT-facing runbooks and triage scripts used at first contact, and train the help desk on each application before it launches. Serve as the escalation point for internal customer issues IT cannot resolve — coordinating with engineering on root cause, workarounds, and permanent fixes, and closing the loop with the affected users. Support the Chief of AI and Autonomy in building and executing the transition roadmap as the organization matures its operational support model for AI applications — tracking phases, milestones, and readiness criteria, and flagging risks to the handoff of operational ownership from engineering to steady-state operations. Partner with factory NOC staff to define how each released AI application is monitored and supported in production: service catalog entries, health dashboards, alert thresholds and routing, on-call rotations, and escalation paths. Help coordinate across the internal AI research lab, data center operations, engineering, and Corporate IT to document clear ownership (RACI) for applications, models, and the compute and network infrastructure they run on, so nothing falls between teams during the transition. Write NOC-facing runbooks, standard operating procedures, and incident playbooks for every application; prepare and facilitate transition readiness reviews and tabletop exercises before each responsibility moves. Help put incident, problem, and change management practices in place with the NOC — post-incident reviews, change calendars, and planned-maintenance communications to internal customers — so users experience the transition as continuity, not disruption. Analyze support tickets and self-help usage to identify recurring failure patterns, feeding documentation updates, UX fixes, and backlog items that measurably reduce ticket volume over time. Establish and report service metrics for the portfolio: first-contact resolution, time-to-resolution, self-service deflection, documentation coverage, and user satisfaction. Own the documentation system itself — information architecture, style guide, templates, review cadence, and version control — so content stays accurate as applications evolve release over release.
